general.md: LayoutBuilder gives "sizing information based on the specific spot in the widget tree"; "imagine a custom widget, where you want the sizing to be based on the space specifically given to that widget, and not the app window in general. In this scenario, use `LayoutBuilder`."

issues.text: Section 4 says constraints are the smallest and largest width and height, then the builder reads constraints.maxWidth. I guess maxWidth is the largest width, but the text never says so, and the whole decision depends on it.
issues.quote: The builder reads `constraints.maxWidth`, compares it with a width the team chose
issues.fix: Change to "The builder reads `constraints.maxWidth`, the largest width the parent allows, compares it with a width the team chose".

issues.text: Section 4 and the diagram say both subtrees use "the same piece, ProductTile", but what ProductTile is only arrives in section 5. I read section 4 guessing.
issues.fix: Change to "Both use the same piece, `ProductTile`, the widget that shows one product's name and price." and drop the duplicate sentence at the start of section 5's prose.

issues.text: The grid branch wraps crossAxisCount and mainAxisExtent in gridDelegate: SliverGridDelegateWithFixedCrossAxisCount(...). The prose explains the two arguments but never says what gridDelegate or that long name is, so I stop on "Sliver" and wonder if it matters.
issues.fix: Add after "`crossAxisCount` is that column count": "; both are passed through `gridDelegate`, the setting that tells the `GridView` how many columns to use and how tall each tile is."

issues.text: "the usual page wrappers" assumes I have met MaterialApp, Scaffold and Center before; none is in what I know. I can skip them, but "usual" makes me feel I missed a lesson.
issues.quote: `MaterialApp`, `Scaffold` and `Center` are the usual page wrappers.
issues.fix: Replace with "`MaterialApp`, `Scaffold` and `Center` only set up a page around the catalog; they do not change its width here."

issues.text: The test is said to run "without a device", then two paragraphs later there is a "test screen" 800 pixels wide. I have to stop and reconcile: what screen, if there is no device?
issues.quote: The test screen is 800 pixels wide by default
issues.fix: Change the first sentence to "builds the catalog without a real device, on a pretend screen the test sets up", so the later "test screen" refers back to it.

issues.text: "the same two tiles" comes from nowhere: the test's products list is outside the shown lines, so I only learn there are two products by reverse-reading findsNWidgets(2).
issues.quote: At 900 it gets 800, still wide enough for a grid holding the same two tiles.
issues.fix: Add before that sentence: "The test's `products` list holds two products."

issues.text: Misconception 2 is not something I would believe. I might think one fixed width that looks good on my phone is safe everywhere, not that "predictable is what responsive means".
issues.quote: Using a fixed pixel width for every widget makes a layout more predictable, and predictable is what responsive means.
issues.fix: Rephrase to: "If I pick a fixed width that looks good on my phone, it will look fine on every screen." (and update the matching quiz q2 misconception text).

issues.text: Explanation d says Flutter apps "run natively"; "natively" is not a word I know and the lesson never says where Flutter apps run. I can still reject d, but the explanation does not help.
issues.quote: Flutter apps also run natively on phones and tablets.
issues.fix: Reword to "Flutter apps also run as ordinary apps on phones and tablets, with no browser involved."

issues.text: Explanation d says "The products are a plain list in the test", but the lesson never shows the test's products, so this explanation tells me something I cannot check from the text.
issues.quote: The products are a plain list in the test; nothing is loaded.
issues.fix: Reword to "The test only checks which widgets the catalog builds for a width; nothing about loading products is involved."
